chapter: With Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, 1936-39
title: Webb's trip back to Baltimore and his family
summary: McRae recounts Webb driving home for his operation and answers Welburn's questions about his wife, sister and pictures.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Because he went to John Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore. He left me in Washington. He was driving back. He sat right in front of Keyes Restaurant, there at 7th and T. Well that's the eatery -- famous eatery place, Keyes Restaurant. That's 7th and T in Washington, D.C. Around the corner from the theater. And he was telling me, "Anything happen to me -- if I don't see you no more" -- "Come on now, I'm not kidding. I'm

just tell you, (inaudible) Chick." "Come on, ain't nothing going to happen." He say, "Nah, nah, nah (inaudible), you take care of Ella (inaudible)." "Take care of the band. Take care of Ella (inaudible)." I say, "Okay, I will see you -- go on back and have the operation and I'll see you in Florida somewhere. In four or five days you would join us." (Inaudible), "I'll be down there." "If I don't see you -- you know, don't kid me now -- He got on in his ear (inaudible)." I hollered at (inaudible) his wife, "All right, I'll see yall later." Gone (inaudible) on back up there.
Did he have brothers and sisters?

There was something I was trying to get from you for that interview. I want to get some pictures for you from her.
I want to get you the pictures from the paper of the funeral down there. (These are some dramatic things) I think it would be something you would like to have -- or some write-ups on him from that.
And there's some other pictures on Ella -- some very good pictures on Chick Webb I want to get for you.
